exposure: Type of childbirth-associated injury (vesicovaginal fistula, rectovaginal fistula, perineal tear)
outcome: Successful resolution of incontinence after repair
cohort: The cohort consisted of 481 women, aged 14-71 years, presenting with incontinence secondary to childbirth-associated injuries in remote Democratic Republic of Congo for surgical repair during outreach campaigns.
finding: Vesicovaginal fistulas were the predominant childbirth injury, with poorly managed vaginal deliveries being the leading cause, and they were less likely to result in successful resolution of incontinence after repair compared to rectovaginal fistulas and perineal tears.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery (53.9%), caesarean section (25.0%), and laparotomy (hysterectomy) (21.2%) were identified as causes of the fistulas, with poorly managed vaginal deliveries being the leading cause.
